subject: Headcount runway triage — OKR-linked req prioritization for QBR
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Headcount runway triage — OKR-linked req prioritization for QBR

Team —

QBR prep next week has one tight ask from execs: give a prioritized list of reqs we will (a) commit to hire in Q2, (b) backfill immediately if vacated, or (c) defer/cancel to hit our cost target. I uploaded a starting matrix (attached) with owners and OKR tags.

Quick context:
- OKR revenue: two infra and two feature hires are directly linked to the "Latency->Conversion" initiative.
- OKR platform: one senior infra req and one reliability PM are nice-to-have but could be deferred.

Action items (please):
- Open the attached QBR_headcount_matrix.xlsx and set each row to APPROVE / BACKFILL / DEFER with a 1-line rationale.
- Highlight any hiring freeze exceptions you need (role + justification + customer impact).
- Return updates within 48 hours — EOD Thu 11 Feb.

We need a clean slide for the QBR deck listing approved reqs and the immediate budget delta. Markus, can you preview cost impact if we approve the backfills vs deferrals?

Thanks —
Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com
Attachment: QBR_headcount_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Headcount runway triage — OKR-linked req prioritization for QBR

+1 to Maya's ask and I've filled my rows in the matrix (see attached comments). High-level thoughts:

- Infrastructure team: propose DEFERRING two junior infra hires (infra-eng-3, infra-eng-4). We can cover 80% of planned work with contractors for the next 3 months — cheaper runway and keeps critical delivery intact. I flagged infra-eng-1 (senior) as APPROVE — that one is blocker for the KV-cache refactor.
- Feature squad: approve one growth engineer (growth-eng-2) that maps directly to the latency->conversion OKR.

Customer note: Capstone Health deployment has a go-live dependency on the KV-cache refactor. If we defer the senior infra hire, Capstone will ask for a timeline extension — I started a parallel thread with capstone-ops@capstonehealth.com to set expectations.

FYI — I updated the matrix with two backfill requests marked APPROVE:
- CS Manager (backfill) — justified: ongoing enterprise renewals with Acme and Capstone in March/April; losing runway here risks renewal discounts and exec churn.
- Integration Engineer (backfill) — justified: the AcmeRetail integration requires immediate attention; this role is a direct dependency (customer has given a firm go date).

I'm OK deferring one product designer (design-2) for this quarter; low immediate impact on OKRs.

Please note: I'll need written approval for the two backfills to present to procurement (I copied acme-procurement@acme.com on internal procurement steps in a separate mail).

Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Customer Success
vanessa@redwood.com
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Headcount runway triage — OKR-linked req prioritization for QBR

Thanks — I reviewed the matrix and ran a quick cost delta model (attached req_cost_model_2027.csv). High level:

- Approving two backfills (CS Manager, Integration Engineer) increases run-rate by ~$52k / month.
- Deferring the two junior infra hires saves ~$34k / month but introduces contractor spend ~ $12k / month for the 3-month bridge. Net savings if we defer = ~$22k / month for Q2.

Recommendation: approve the two customer-facing backfills (Vanessa) to keep ACV and renewal momentum; defer the two junior infra hires and convert to short-term contractor coverage for 3 months. Approve the senior infra hire (infra-eng-1) as Jonas requested.

I'll note this in the cost slide and produce a single number for the QBR that shows net run-rate delta and the staged-phased hiring plan.

Attachment: req_cost_model_2027.csv

-Markus
Markus Klein

Subject: Final: QBR headcount decisions & runway plan (condensed)

Thanks everyone — consolidating decisions for the QBR deck and procurement:

Decisions (final):
- APPROVE: CS Manager (backfill) — owner: Vanessa; immediate start for renewal coverage.
- APPROVE: Integration Engineer (backfill) — owner: Vanessa; critical for AcmeRetail go-live.
- APPROVE: Senior infra (infra-eng-1) — owner: Jonas; blocker for KV-cache refactor.
- DEFER: two junior infra hires (infra-eng-3, infra-eng-4) -> cover with contractors for 3 months.
- DEFER: Product Designer (design-2) for Q2.

Cost summary: Markus will include the net run-rate delta on slide 3 (approx +$30k/month after contractor offsets).

Next steps:
- Vanessa: share procurement request and doc: acme-procurement@acme.com is copied.
- Jonas: confirm contractor name/estimate (sarah@consultants.io) by EOD Thu.
- Markus: attach single-line cost delta to the QBR slide deck.

Attachment: qbr_final_headcount_slide.pdf

Short approvals received:
> Laura Bennett: "Approved for the two backfills."
> Jonas Weber: "Ack — approve senior hire and deferrals as noted."

If no objections by EOD Thu, I'll lock this in for the QBR pack.
